@graph.name: How to Hire a Senior Python Developer
@graph.description: A step-by-step guide to hiring and onboarding a senior Python developer for your FastAPI, Django, or AI backend project.

step.name: Define your Python project requirements
step.text: Identify: REST API vs. async backend, AI/LangChain integration needs, background task requirements (Celery), database (PostgreSQL/MongoDB), and deployment target (Docker/Kubernetes/AWS). A one-page spec prevents scope creep and speeds up developer evaluation.

step.name: Screen for FastAPI + Pydantic v2 + type annotation expertise
step.text: Check the candidate's GitHub: Are all Python files fully typed with mypy annotations? Do they use Pydantic v2 (not v1)? Do they use SQLAlchemy 2.0 async sessions? Are there pytest test files with real assertions? No type annotations from a 'senior' Python developer is a hard disqualifier in 2026.

step.name: Assign a paid technical test
step.text: Give a 2-3 hour paid test: build a FastAPI endpoint with Pydantic v2 validation, async SQLAlchemy query, JWT authentication, and a pytest test. This reveals code quality, async patterns, and testing habits more accurately than any interview question.

step.name: Assess async Python and Celery knowledge
step.text: Ask: How do you avoid blocking the FastAPI event loop? A senior developer explains asyncio.run_in_executor(), Celery offloading for heavy tasks, and async SQLAlchemy session management. Ask about their Alembic migration workflow and how they handle zero-downtime schema changes.

step.name: Agree on contract, milestones, and deliverables
step.text: Use milestone-based contracts: Discovery/OpenAPI spec → Core API → Auth + Models → Celery tasks → Testing → Docker + CI/CD → Handover. Each milestone has written acceptance criteria. Insist on: all code committed to your GitHub, pytest suite with coverage report, and Alembic migrations committed.

step.name: Handover and documentation
step.text: The final deliverable includes: source code to your GitHub, OpenAPI/Swagger docs, Docker Compose for local development, Alembic migration history, pytest test suite with coverage report, runbook for deployment and monitoring, and a 60-minute walkthrough session.

mainEntity.name: What is FastAPI and why should I hire a FastAPI developer?

acceptedAnswer.text: FastAPI is a modern Python web framework for building high-performance APIs. Built on Starlette + Pydantic v2. Key advantages: automatic OpenAPI docs, async-first design, Pydantic request/response validation, and type safety throughout. It's the right choice for any new Python API backend in 2026.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to hire a Python developer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rates by experience: Junior: $20–$50/hr. Mid-level: $50–$100/hr. Senior: $80–$200/hr. Monthly retainer with Ramesh Das (6+ years FastAPI/Django): $1,999/mo for 160 hours — significantly below equivalent agency rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the best Python frameworks to look for when hiring?

acceptedAnswer.text: Framework priorities in 2026: FastAPI (must-have for API work), Django (for admin-heavy platforms), Pydantic v2 (insist on v2 not v1), SQLAlchemy 2.0 (async ORM), LangChain/LlamaIndex (AI features), pytest (no exceptions), Celery (background tasks). Red flag: Flask for new production APIs.

mainEntity.name: How do Python developers handle database migrations in production?

acceptedAnswer.text: The standard tool is Alembic (for SQLAlchemy) or Django's built-in migrations. Professional workflow: never modify production database manually, generate migrations with alembic revision --autogenerate, test on a copy of production data, apply migrations before deploying new code, keep rollback migrations ready.

mainEntity.name: What is Celery and when do I need it in a Python project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Celery is a Python distributed task queue for background operations. You need it for: sending emails, processing uploaded files, AI inference (don't block the web server for 30-second GPU tasks), scheduled jobs, and webhook processing. Celery + Redis is the standard Python pattern for background task processing.
